prize_parts.citation: for experimental demonstration of the physical principles governing long-range electron transfer through proteins

statement.case_for: I keep B028 first after reading all eight openings. Gray and Winkler showed, with engineered and native proteins, that electron tunnelling over 10-25 angstroms follows quantitative rules in distance, driving force and reorganization energy, and that the intervening protein medium tunes the rate. This takes Marcus theory into biology and gives a physical mechanism for the electron transfer steps of respiration and photosynthesis. It has been confirmed independently for more than three decades and is textbook material, so the question is not maturity. It is one coherent achievement with a clean two-person credit, which leaves room under the three-person limit, and it is chemistry in the plain sense of explaining how a chemical process works in living systems. I recognise that I am the only member who ranked it, so the discussion should test it against the better-supported candidates and not assume it carries.
statement.case_against: No colleague ranked B028 in the opening round. The strongest objection is attribution and novelty. The field was built by many hands, including Dutton and Moser on natural systems, Beratan and Onuchic on tunnelling-pathway theory, and Marcus, who was recognised in 1992. A prize to Gray and Winkler could be read as crediting a line of work and not a single discovery, and it may be seen as late and as lacking the broad practical reach of base editing, sequencing or degraders. My own research is close to this field, so my enthusiasm may overstate its standing with the wider committee.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B034 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, arguing that targeted degradation turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction and that the cereblon mechanism explains molecular glues.
responses.response: I agree that B034 is the best-supported candidate and that the mechanism is well confirmed. I disagree with putting Handa in the same trio as the PROTAC pair. The cereblon and thalidomide discovery is a separate achievement from the PROTAC concept. A three-person set that spans both is a compromise that credits neither branch in full. I would rather the committee settle first whether this is one discovery or two, and the expert reports should speak to that. On the PROTAC branch alone I find Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work more decisive for the modern field than the molecular-glue attribution, which is why I proposed Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks massively parallel sequencing first and proposes only Balasubramanian and Klenerman, because the Solexa reversible-terminator chemistry is the cleanest and most defensible attribution under the three-person cap.
responses.response: I accept that the Cambridge pair is the cleanest configuration and that B011 is fully mature. My reservation is that the field's commercial history, with 454, Solexa and the Mayer colony-amplification work, is entangled with patent and priority claims, so we should see what the expert reports say about which step is the chemical invention. Johan is right that the cap pushes towards two names. I would resist adding Rothberg merely to fill a third place. B011 stays a serious alternative for me, but I would still put the electron-transfer physics first on scientific grounds.

responses.point: Zou ranks B042, serial femtosecond crystallography, third, with Chapman, Fromme and Hajdu, crediting Hajdu with the diffraction-before-destruction concept.
responses.response: I ranked B042 second and share the view that it opens samples that could not be studied before. Our trios differ at the third place. I put Schlichting there for time-resolved enzymology, while Zou puts Hajdu there for the original concept. The Neutze and Hajdu proposal is a real priority question, and the expert reports should settle whether the concept or the experimental realisation is the decisive achievement. I also see a risk in the argument that this is a method prize. Its chemical weight depends on time-resolved results that are still maturing, so I would not rank it above a candidate with settled consequences.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranks nanopore sequencing first on a clean physical principle, ionic current blockade through a molecular constriction, but notes that living status of some credited names may constrain the configuration.
responses.response: I share the appeal of a clear physical principle and think B001 is mature and timely. The credit issue is serious. Branton is deceased, and Heiner's recollection about Bayley should be checked before the committee relies on it, because eligibility for a prize could change the whole configuration. Even setting that aside, five credited contributors and a split between the translocation concept, pore engineering and enzyme ratcheting make this hard to reduce to three. I would want the attribution cleared before supporting it over B034.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports support B028 as a single attributable discovery or as a line of work spread across Gray, Winkler, Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic.
Whether B034 should be read as one achievement or as two, the PROTAC concept and the cereblon and molecular-glue discovery, which decides who can sit in a three-person set.
Whether the clinical record for degraders, with no approved PROTAC, makes B034 premature for this year.
For B042, whether the concept (Hajdu, Neutze) or the experimental realisation (Chapman, Fromme, Schlichting) is treated as decisive.
statement.conflict_note: My own research on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes is close to B028 and to the proton-coupled electron transfer candidate, so I flag proximity of field, not a personal tie, and I will rely on the expert reports. The provided profile shows no personal or institutional connection to Gray or Winkler. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose first-ranked candidate is B051, and the committee may note that connection, though I do not see a conflict in it.
